description: Issue #742, the profile-INACTIVE direction: byte-for-byte the same source as `heritage-alias-redefinition-rejected-when-active`, checked under Core alone, is completely clean. Without `heritage` claimed, `pr`/`bf`/`bl`/`se` and the nine turtle aliases are ordinary names that register nothing, so the shipped checker accepts a declaration of any of them — exactly as `define ask` is accepted without Sprites. SCOPE, CORRECTED: maintainer ruling #833 (merged as #875) retracted the profile gate for the NAMING axis. `spec/grammar.md:408` makes every profile's primitives -- and every alias spelling of one -- built-in names unconditionally, so a conforming 0.4.0 implementation must raise `ol-reserved-word` here with or without the profile. `spec/tooling.md:175-176` gates which names are AVAILABLE (the `ol-unknown-command` axis) and does not gate the reserved-word rule; the earlier reading of it here conflated the two axes. This fixture therefore pins SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR the spec now contradicts, and is kept red-flagged rather than deleted so the behaviour is not silently unpinned; issue #841 lands the always-on built-in-names list and flips this expectation. Sharing one source with the rejecting sibling is deliberate — it removes the possibility that the two fixtures diverge and the gate silently stops being tested. `"check": true` for the same reason as the sibling: this is a checker rule with no execution.
